title: Let a filesystem finish work before the FUSE_DESTROY reply
body:
fuser replies to `FUSE_DESTROY` first and calls `Filesystem::destroy()` after that. For a filesystem that buffers changes and writes them out later, that order comes too late. The kernel completes `umount` as soon as it gets the reply. On a `fuseblk` mount the device claim goes away at the same moment, and udisks tells the user the disk is safe to remove. Anything `destroy()` writes after that races with the user pulling the disk, or with another program opening the device exclusively.

I hit this with a copy-on-write filesystem for removable disks that publishes changes in batches. A test detached the device right after `umount` returned and killed the daemon. The last batch was lost, even though `umount` had reported success.

The fix I use adds one callback with a no-op default:

```rust
/// Finish work that must complete before acknowledging `FUSE_DESTROY`.
fn before_destroy(&self) {}
```

The session loop calls it right before it replies to DESTROY. While it runs, `umount` waits and the mount still owns the device. Cleanup stays in `destroy()`, which still runs after the session threads end. The callback does not run when the connection aborts without a DESTROY.

It takes `&self` because the worker threads still share the filesystem at that point. `destroy(&mut self)` only gets exclusive access once they have ended.

The implementation, with a test that the reply waits for the callback, is https://github.com/painhardcore/fuser/commit/0b438b0. It applies cleanly to current master and the test passes there. I've run it since late September in my pipelines.
